newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares in holding pattern with Europe.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares in holding pattern with Europe.

text.p: Belgian shares, which had a mildly bumpy ride on Thursday but nevertheless held on to light gains at the close, are expected to maintain a holding pattern with other European bourses, traders said.
"The problem is the volume. It just isn't there. Until it comes back this market is going nowhere," one trader said.
Leading Belgian retailer Delhaize, due to report first half results on Friday, was the volume leader rising 3.4 percent to 1,665 francs on a turnover of 86,221 shares.
Traders reported one big buyer of the stock. They could give no explanation. Net profit is seen 15 to 22.5 percent up.
Polyurethane foam maker Recticel, which on Wednesday reported first half losses of 233 million francs against a profit of 192 million in the comparable 1995 period, was the day's main gainer.
The shares soared 6.1 percent to 280 francs. Traders said the first half loss was less than expected.

Trading in the shares of film finisher Spector Photo Group NV was suspended until Monday after a report in De Financieel-Economische Tijd -- which the firm did not deny -- that it was planning a one billion franc capital increase in October to finance recent acquisitions abroad.

Earlier this year, Spector bought a majority stake in Porst a Swiss photo group with operations in Germany and Hungaria. It also acquired 100 percent of Interdiscount France from Swiss group Interdiscount.

Spector, which is holding a conference with analysts and reporters on Friday to explain its intentions, formally denied -- without giving details -- elements of the article relating to the acquisitions.
The Bel-20 share index ended Thursday with gains of 6.70 points or 0.39 percent in a 1,736.13/1,726.24 range. Total market volume was just one billion francs.

Traders noted that the index had edged slightly higher in very quiet morning business before dropping into negative territory after a sharp fall in U.S. weekly jobless claim figures and then climbing back again with the rest of Europe.
They said all eyes would be on the August non-farm payroll figures due on Friday.
